assessment: Major: invalid core moment-growth derivation in P5; P1-P4 and P6 remain Minor in their bounded scopes; no false main theorem demonstrated

problems.title: The auxiliary lower bound and finite critical points require qualifications
source_locators: Theorem 1.4(i), equation (19), and following paragraph, p. 6
Nonconstant environment factor in proof, p. 19
hypotheses: IID real environment with all absolute exponential moments; nearest-neighbor simple random walk
d >= 3; weak disorder; nonzero continuous compactly supported test f
Theorem 1.4 explicitly drops upper-boundedness and beta > beta_L2; beta=0 remains permitted
problems.decisive_evidence: At beta=0 with any nonconstant bounded IID environment, W_n=1, X_n^f=0, a(p)=0, q*=infinity. With 1/infinity=0 the probability in (19) is one rather than tending to zero; without that convention the bound is undefined. Independently, choose omega in {0,1}, P(omega=1)=r=(1+pi_d)/2. The exact ratio R_beta=[r+(1-r)e^(-2beta)]/[r+(1-r)e^(-beta)]^2 <= 1/r, and E W_n^2 <= (1-pi_d)/(1-pi_d/r) for all finite beta. Thus beta_L2 and beta_cr can both be infinite even for nonconstant bounded weights.
problems.independent_computation: Exact boundary calculation and symbolic verification of the cleared Bernoulli-ratio inequality in independent_checks.py; transience, geometric meeting law and L2/zero-one argument proved in independent_analytic_evidence.md.
problems.counterevidence: The main Theorem 1.1 assumes beta>beta_L2 and excludes both counterexamples. The proof invokes a nonconstant factor, indicating an intended qualification. Junk-Lacoin v3 p.3 explicitly permits infinite critical temperatures.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem 1.4(i) is the auxiliary fluctuation lower bound; Theorem A supplies the stated model range.
problems.repair: Require nonconstant normalized eta for the nontrivial lower bound. Then q* is finite by a favorable finite-box event and killed-walk spectral radius. Permit extended critical values and qualify finite strict-gap assertions.
problems.impact_boundary: The literal auxiliary boundary assertion and finite-critical-point background assertions are false as printed. This is not a counterexample to the nondegenerate beyond-L2 main theorem.

problems.title: Gaussian covariance is inconsistent with nearest-neighbor normalization
hypotheses: Nearest-neighbor simple random walk on Z^d, d>=3
Endpoint scaled by sqrt(n); phi explicitly called standard normal
At beta=0 the bounded continuous test f(x)=cos(x_1) is admissible
problems.decisive_evidence: The exact expectation is [1-(1-cos(1/sqrt(n)))/d]^n -> exp(-1/(2d)), not exp(-1/2). One-step covariance is I_d/d.
problems.independent_computation: Exact characteristic-function derivation and independent numerical convergence at d=3 to 0.8464817249 versus 0.6065306597.
problems.counterevidence: An informal convention for standard might explain the notation; constant covariance changes do not change polynomial fluctuation exponents.
problems.core_dependency: The CLT convolution used to select z and define the good event in Lemma 2.6.
problems.repair: Use phi_d=(d/(2pi))^(d/2)exp(-d|x|^2/2), or consistently rescale the walk. Reselect z with f*phi_d(z) nonzero; the Gaussian Fourier transform gives existence.
problems.impact_boundary: Incorrect literal covariance and associated convolution; existence of a valid z and the fluctuation exponent survive.

problems.title: The fractional-moment domain in Proposition 2.1 is overstated
source_locators: Statement that Section 2.1 is valid regardless of dimension/disorder, p.8
hypotheses: p in (0,1) explicitly included in proof
IID weights with all exponential moments; section not restricted to weak disorder
Counterexample d=1, standard Gaussian weights, beta=4, p=1/2
problems.decisive_evidence: For p<1 the correct Jensen bounds are lambda(p beta)-p lambda(beta) <= a(p) <= 0. Expanding over 2^n paths gives a(1/2) <= (log 2)/2-2 < 0, whereas a(0)=a(1)=0, contradicting nondecreasing behavior on R_+.
problems.independent_computation: Independent exact Gaussian moment algebra and path-concavity proof; superadditivity gives existence of the fractional limit.
problems.counterevidence: The later q* argument only needs p>=1, suggesting the intended restriction.
problems.core_dependency: Moment-rate properties preceding q* and the exceptional-site construction.
problems.repair: Restrict nonnegative bounds and monotonicity to p>=1; give reversed fractional bounds separately.
problems.impact_boundary: A false stated range; no resulting failure of the q* argument or final theorem.

problems.title: The general lower-bound proof needs a moment replacement and local sign/geometry corrections
source_locators: Lemma 2.6, pp.13-15, including Holder event on p.15
Grid count pp.15-16; event inclusion p.18
Equation (64), p.21; selection density and heat kernel p.22
hypotheses: d>=3; weak disorder; general nonzero signed f in C_c
The general lower-bound theorem does not assume p*>1, whereas the proof chooses p in (1,p*)
Independent time layers; ell_n=o(sqrt(n)); uniform CLT good-event probabilities over the required window
problems.decisive_evidence: The stated general hypotheses do not justify choosing p>1 below p*. A complete replacement uses uniform integrability: u_n=sup E[W_t 1_Ac] <= R b_n+sup E[W_t 1_{W_t>R}] ->0. Conditional Markov with h_n=sqrt(u_n)+n^-1 reduces (44)-(47) to the existing lower-tail lemma. For f<=0 the printed event Zhat<=positive is automatic and cannot imply a small-absolute-amplitude event.
problems.independent_computation: Root analytic derivation of the UI replacement, signed concentration identity Q_cY(u)=Q_Y(u/|c|), d-dimensional grid ratio O(n^-d delta/2), and stretched-exponential heat-kernel domination; complete details in independent_analytic_evidence.md.
problems.counterevidence: For the main bounded-environment theorem, Theorem B already supplies p*>1. Later Junk-Lacoin Corollary 2.8 gives p*>1 under more general weak disorder. Absolute truncation errors in the source support the signed repair.
problems.core_dependency: General lower bound Theorem 1.4(i), then main exponent after p*=q*.
problems.repair: Use UI or explicitly justify p*>1; use bad event A^c in Holder; use |Zhat|. Use xi_q until p*=q*, probability >3/4 before (35), C(1+n^((1-delta)/2)/ell_n)^d grid count, E_n subset Ehat_n, constants covering E|eta-1| and E[eta|eta-1|], full chosen-site indicator/translated block in the density, and heat kernel C(Delta t)^(-d/2)exp(-c|Delta x|^2/Delta t).
problems.impact_boundary: Several invalid displayed steps, with explicit repairs preserving exponents and conditional independence. No nondegenerate positive-beta counterexample to the conclusion was obtained.

problems.title: The moment-growth exponent and renewal coordinates are incorrect as displayed
hypotheses: Weak disorder beyond L2 with upper-bounded weights; 1<p*<2
Doob exponent must lie strictly between 1 and p*
problems.decisive_evidence: The printed lambda=p*(1-eta/2) yields lambda(2+eta)=p*(2-eta^2/2)<2p*, not the claimed exponent 2(p*+delta). At p*=3/2, eta=1/2 the power is 45/16<3. The renewal definitions omit cumulative time and position, although (97) uses absolute coordinates.
problems.independent_computation: Executed symbolic identity and example in independent_checks.py; full admissible-exponent, joint-event and renewal reconstruction in independent_analytic_evidence.md.
problems.counterevidence: An admissible replacement lambda exists for every p*>1 and eta>0. Later Junk-Lacoin independently states p*=q*; it does not validate the printed algebra.
problems.core_dependency: Lemma 4.7 feeds Theorem 1.5 (p*=q*) and the main fluctuation exponent.
problems.repair: Set L=max(1,2p*/(2+eta)), lambda=(p*+L)/2 and delta=[lambda(2+eta)-2p*]/2>0; bound the joint stopping event and union over levels. In Theorem 1.5 choose eta=min(epsilon/[2(p*+epsilon+1)],(p*-1)/2), retain gain alpha^(2k-l-1), and define cumulative sigma_{i+1}=sigma_i+sigma shifted and Z_{i+1}=Z_i+Z shifted. Fresh time layers then give the required exponential moment base.
problems.impact_boundary: Invalid core derivation as printed; the displayed complete repair preserves its conclusion conditional on localization/tail lemmas. No false final theorem established.
problems.severity_rationale: The wrong exponent is smaller than 2p*, so the bound cannot beat the alpha^(-2kp*) scale required in the proof of Theorem 1.5. This materially invalidates the acquired core derivation of p*=q*, used to identify the main fluctuation exponent. The explicit repair and later independent result limit the conclusion to the proof, without reducing a core derivation defect to Minor solely because a repair exists.

problems.title: Upper bounds and overlap moments require normalized constants
source_locators: Lemma 4.3, pp.27-28, including overshoot (79) on p.28
Standing normalization and upper-bound assumptions, pp.1-3
hypotheses: For the full-range witness start from any nondegenerate admissible main-theorem model and shift by its upper bound
problems.decisive_evidence: The true step bound is W_{n+1}<=M W_n with M=exp(beta K-lambda(beta)). Shifting an admissible model leaves all normalized quantities/disorder unchanged but makes omega<=0. Since W_1 is nonconstant mean one, P(W_1>1+r)>0; choosing eligible 0<K<log(1+r)/beta contradicts the printed n=0 bound. The two-point numerical law is only an illustration, not a beyond-L2 witness.
problems.independent_computation: Exact shift-invariance argument and independently executed normalized two-point example; direct Jensen/Cauchy-Schwarz overlap calculation gives E[R_m^2|F_{m-1}]<=exp((lambda(8beta)+lambda(-8beta))/2)R_{m-1}^2.
problems.counterevidence: A centered environment would give a nonnegative lambda, but centering is not stated. Later Junk-Lacoin (2.11) uses exactly the normalized factor.
problems.core_dependency: Overshoot and bounded increments in Lemma 4.3; overlap second moment in Lemma 4.5; appendix tail estimate.
problems.repair: Set alpha=2M; lower increments are bounded by -1, sufficient for the exponential supermartingale. Replace appendix e^(beta K) by M, obtaining adequate tail constant (1/2)M^-p*. Retain walk probability in A(x)=(1/(2d))sum eta^2; moments finite under (1).
problems.impact_boundary: False intermediate normalization with explicit constant repair. The printed appendix tail constant is not independently refuted, and the main theorem is not disproved.

independent_acceptance_check.scope: Focused verification of all six existing Problems and counterevidence; no redundant full-paper review

problem_checks.decisive_check: At beta=0 all normalized weights and W equal1, so Xf=0 and a=0; the permitted Theorem1.4(i) event has probability1. With top atom r=(1+pi_d)/2, R_beta<=1/r follows from (1-r)t[2r+(1-2r)t]>=0 on[0,1]; the geometric positive-time meeting law gives a uniform second moment for every finite beta.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: Source p6 expressly drops beta>L2. Both witnesses are excluded from the beyond-L2 main range; the nonconstant eta repair and favorable-box q* finiteness are valid. Later reference p3 allows infinite thresholds.

problem_checks.decisive_check: A single SRW step has covariance I/d. Its exact cosine characteristic function at scale sqrt(n) tends to exp(-1/(2d)); standard normal gives exp(-1/2). Replacing the Gaussian and reselecting z works because the corrected Fourier transform has no zeros.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: The test is bounded continuous as allowed in TheoremA; no fluctuation power changes. This is a normalization error with a local repair.

problem_checks.decisive_check: For fractional p, path Jensen gives a>=lambda(p beta)-p lambda(beta) and expectation Jensen gives a<=0. In d1 Gaussian beta4,p1/2, path concavity yields a<=log2/2-2<0 while a0=a1=0. Source p8 explicitly includes this range and allows arbitrary disorder/dimension.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: Existence follows by the source superadditivity argument. Restricting monotonicity/nonnegativity to p>=1 preserves the later q* use.

problem_checks.decisive_check: Read the actual conditional CLT and selected-cone construction through p23. UI gives u_n<=R b_n+sup E[W_t1_{W_t>R}]->0; conditioning on the independent last layer and using h_n=sqrt(u_n)+n^-1 gives a vanishing bad mass without p>1. For f<=0 the printed signed small-amplitude event is automatic, but |Zhat| and Q_cY(u)=Q_Y(u/|c|) give the intended bound. Recomputed grid ratio O(n^(-d delta/2)), reversed E/Ehat inclusion, constant for newly included pathsite eta, full selected-good indicator and shifted time block, and heat-kernel ratio n^(5delta/6). The selected-good indicator is fixed on integrated coordinates; remaining density factors decrease, supporting the stated FKG direction.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: The main upper-bounded setting already has p*>1 by TheoremB. The moment omission concerns the broader auxiliary range; the remaining sign/count/constant corrections retain the same exponents and conditional independence. No false nondegenerate conclusion claimed. Later Cor2.8 supports the conclusion but is not a retrospective proof.

problem_checks.decisive_check: The exact printed lambda=p*(1-eta/2) gives lambda(2+eta)-2p*=-p*eta^2/2<0. At p*=3/2,eta=1/2 it is45/16<3. Thus Lemma4.7 does not beat the alpha^(-2kp*) lower-tail probability explicitly used on p33 to derive Theorem1.5 and hence the main exponent. The joint stopping event and cumulative renewal coordinates are also required by the actual p32-33 definitions.
problem_checks.independent_repair_check: L=max(1,2p*/(2+eta))<p*, lambda=(p*+L)/2 gives1<lambda<p* and delta=[lambda(2+eta)-2p*]/2>0. Strong Markov/fresh layers bound the joint event and its k-fold union. Taking eta additionally <=(p*-1)/2 permits the later Doob exponent. Missing threshold factor alpha and cumulative time/space additions yield a constant adjustment and genuinely independent positive-duration renewals. With m=floor(n/T), their sum<=n and gain base C/k*alpha^(k epsilon/2)>1.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: An invalid core derivation warrants Major without a false final theorem. The explicit segment repair remains conditional on retained localization/tail dependencies. Later reference Cor2.11 states p*=q*; it does not validate the old algebra. No new review of every Yoshida theorem claimed.

problem_checks.result: Verified; Minor retained; locator corrected to pp27-28
problem_checks.decisive_check: Normalized step factor is M=exp(beta K-lambda(beta)). A deterministic shift of any nondegenerate admissible bounded main-regime environment preserves W/disorder but permits a small positive K and contradicts the unnormalized bound on an event W1>1+r. Alpha=2M restores overshoots; the actual lower martingale increment is >=-1, sufficient for a bounded-increment exponential supermartingale. Retaining1/(2d) in A and applying Jensen then Cauchy-Schwarz gives the finite exp((lambda(8beta)+lambda(-8beta))/2) bound.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: No centering assumption is present. Later equation2.11 has the normalized factor. The illustrative two-point law alone is not a beyond-L2 witness; no falsity of the appendix tail constant or final theorem inferred.
